dedupe_keys.name: phmsa pipeline incident and accident data with flagged incident files gas distribution transmission and gathering lng and hazardous liquid us

description: Under 49 CFR Parts 191 and 195, US pipeline operators must report pipeline incidents and accidents to the PHMSA Office of Pipeline Safety within 30 days. PHMSA publishes these reports for gas distribution, gas transmission and gathering, LNG facilities and hazardous liquid pipelines. The metadata, published by PHMSA on the federal data catalogue, states that the reports include the time and location of each incident, injuries and fatalities, commodity spilled or gas released, causes of failure and evacuation procedures, and are used for trends at national, state and operator level; the listing is updated monthly and was modified on 17 September 2026. A companion set of flagged files, starting in 1992, adds fields PHMSA uses for analysis and 20-year trends: serious incidents with a fatality or in-patient injury, significant incidents meeting property damage, spill volume or fire and explosion thresholds, all reported incidents, consequences and state-based reports. Data are available as free ZIP downloads from the PHMSA site, marked public domain. Coverage is the United States. Caveats: reporting criteria have changed over time, and the PHMSA pages refused automated reading on the day, so details come from the PHMSA metadata on data.gov and data.transportation.gov. Simulation uses are pipeline failure frequencies by cause and commodity for fragility and risk models and event catalogues for resilience studies. Related records: data-npms-national-pipeline-mapping-system gives pipeline locations; data-phmsa-pipeline-operator-annual-report-data gives mileage; data-pipeline-grid-cyber-physical-incident-panel builds on these reports.
